name: Trackside Core
description: The settings and the paintings page for the Trackside widgets (trackside_photo, trackside_plate, trackside_lineup, trackside_scene): the Transport Victoria key, the fal.ai key, the contact for Wikimedia Commons and the daily painting budget. No widget of its own.

settings.name: vic_key
settings.label: Transport Victoria open data key
settings.help: For Melbourne's trains and trams. Free: sign up at https://opendata.transport.vic.gov.au, then make an API key under your account. It is sent only to api.opendata.transport.vic.gov.au, in the KeyID header. Not needed for the other places or a feed of your own.

settings.name: fal_api_key
settings.label: fal.ai API key (AI paintings)
settings.help: With a key the widgets can paint each vehicle from her photograph, at about US$0.04 a painting, once per vehicle and style. Leave it blank to use the key under Settings › Generative AI. Without either the widgets show photographs.

settings.name: contact
settings.label: Contact for Wikimedia Commons
settings.help: An email address or a web page, sent in the widget's User-Agent as Wikimedia asks of every application that reads its API. The widget names its own project page by default.

settings.name: gen_daily_usd
settings.label: Painting budget per day
settings.help: The most the widgets may spend on new paintings in a day, at the models' listed prices. 0 is no limit, within the ceiling under Settings › Generative AI. Paintings are kept, so a vehicle in a style only costs once; a class painted from a class photograph is shared by every vehicle of that class.

settings.name: gen_per_refresh
settings.label: New paintings started per preview
settings.help: How many new paintings one settled preview in the editor may start (1 to 50). A panel's own render starts what its page needs, within the daily budget.

settings.name: gen_parallel
settings.label: Paintings made at once
settings.help: How many paintings fal.ai works on side by side (1 to 8).
